notes: Five alternating-order rounds (order rotated and reversed between rounds) on a shared 4-core VM; no concurrent builds or test jobs owned by this experiment. Other host activity was uncontrolled.

Base is PR #671 head a87a3c09; candidate is 55ca2e54 (this branch). Both trees used the same compiler binary (identical SHA-256: the compiler does not use list(bytes), so the runtime.c change does not reach it).
JIT runtime caches primed before timing; default optimization and JIT inlining limit (PYSTACHY_JIT_INLINE unset).
All outputs/checksums agreed across CPython, base and candidate in both modes; repeat checksums compared with timings removed.
Timed workloads include in-loop lazy initialization and cache misses. Whole-process time adds setup, checksums, startup and JIT compilation.
repeat is tools/re_repeat_bench.py 1000 --cpu; each process reports the median of three warmed samples per case.

instruction_counts.tool: valgrind --tool=callgrind (Ir); AOT binaries for base/head, python3.13 -I for cpython
instruction_counts.note: timed_loops = run with loops minus run without loops (setup, checksums and startup cancel). v8_timed is bench/pyperformance/regex_v8.py with the post-loop checksum removed. Callgrind counts each byte of a rep-stosb memset as an instruction, which inflates Pystachy allocation zeroing relative to its time.
